source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Make a video to record below steps and output:
1. AC off & on SUT.
5. Power on SUT, and record the time until BIOS logo shows up.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. BIOS logo should show up within 10 seconds after SUT powers on.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Early video output: early video output verification requires observing the display at the very start of POST (before the OS); a person at the console/display must confirm the early video appears. Agent cannot see the monitor.

original_test_intent: Measure from the approved SUT power-on reference event to the first physical display of the BIOS logo after an AC off/on sequence and confirm the interval is no more than 10 seconds.
original_method: Continuously video-record the approved AC off/on and power-on sequence, synchronize a visible timing reference, observe the intended display output from before power-on, mark first BIOS-logo visibility, and retain recovery logs.
manual_activity: A human must ensure the camera covers the physical early-video path and judge the first frame where the correct BIOS logo becomes visible; software boot timestamps cannot substitute.
required_inputs: Approved AC control method and power-on event
Physical display/output and BIOS logo reference
Maintenance window, workload drain and recovery access
safety_requirements: One authorized-user approval may cover the unchanged AC/power plan.
Drain active workloads and maintain stable, recoverable power control.
ED-32 does not imply physical cord removal here; the project must define the AC method because this source does not.
Stop on failed boot, lost management or incomplete video.
agent_execution_scope: Prepare the timing/evidence plan and synchronize available logs.
Support an approved software-controlled PDU/power action only if the project plan names it; this review runs nothing.
Analyze the supplied video and timestamps, but do not claim the human capture or formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the timer origin, AC method, outage and logo reference.
Operate/observe the physical display and ensure continuous capture.
Review the measured interval/recovery and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correct that SSH cannot prove first physical video output.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain continuous physical video; BMC power timestamps may be synchronized supporting evidence only.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: AC off/on, power on, first BIOS logo, 10-second limit and 30/30-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use continuous high-frame-rate video with a synchronized power-event marker and document the first unambiguous correct-logo frame.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact board/display route and BIOS build.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record camera frame rate, timer source, BMC/BIOS and display-path metadata.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner-supplied platform logo and power-event definition.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines the timing origin and frame-level evidence without changing the 10-second criterion.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: BMC or OS boot logs alone cannot prove physical video visibility.

project_override_considerations: The project may define PDU or another approved AC control and the timing origin. The report must state that method and cannot claim a physical cable-removal test unless that was explicitly required and performed by a human.
expected_evidence: Approved power plan and timer definition

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The skipped step numbering is editorial and does not change the AC/power-on/video intent. The timer origin is underspecified but not contradictory.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Intent and threshold are clear; power, timing and capture details are execution-readiness inputs.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agrees that physical early video is human-observed.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its continuous timing and recovery controls.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Avoids overextending Seq 182 and separates optional automated power support from the manual visual acceptance core.

review_improvement: Makes the 10-second metric reproducible at frame level and prevents an OS/BMC boot timestamp or late-starting video from being accepted as early-video proof.
independent_technical_reasoning: Although power control and timestamp correlation can be automated, the test's defining evidence is first visible BIOS-logo output on a physical display. Human setup/visual judgment is core, so the classification remains MANUAL ONLY.
no_automatic_retry: Do not issue another AC/power cycle after delayed/missing video or boot failure; preserve the full recording and stop.
